2113167718476333567.name: Global Governance Initiative
2113167718476333567.desc: Reposts and versions of foreign ministry material on the Global Governance Initiative (GGI), centred on Wang Yi's 23 October keynote at the 2026 Global Governance Forum in Xiong'an and the follow-up actions he announced.
2113167718476333567.line: China says the world's governance system is unfair and offers its own initiative to reform it.
2113167718476333567.says: PRC accounts present Xi Jinping's Global Governance Initiative as a plan for a "more just and equitable" world order. Around the 23 October forum in Xiong'an they relayed Xi's claim that deficits in peace, development, security and governance are growing, and Wang Yi's eight "practical actions" China says it will take. Foreign voices are quoted praising the initiative.

sample.text: Chinese President Xi Jinping sent a message to the 2026 Global Governance Forum (Xiongan) on Friday. The world is undergoing accelerated transformation unseen in a century, and the deficits in peace, development, security and governance are growing rather than diminishing, Xi…

2113425736040349892.name: 'One Globe, One Community' video
2113425736040349892.desc: A short video on Xi Jinping's idea of a 'community with a shared future for humanity', reposted by embassies and consulates from 23 October.
2113425736040349892.line: A Foreign Ministry video selling Xi's "community with a shared future for humanity".
2113425736040349892.says: Missions reposted a Foreign Ministry video titled "One Globe, One Community". It presents Xi's "community with a shared future for humanity" as a path to mutual respect, fairness, dialogue instead of confrontation, and development for all nations.

sample.text: China’s vision of a community with a shared future for humanity offers a clear path forward. Mutual respect, fairness and justice. Dialogue over confrontation. Development for all. One Globe, One Community.

2112191282000924837.name: Long March 90th anniversary
2112191282000924837.desc: Xi Jinping's remarks marking the 90th anniversary of the Red Army's Long March, shared from 19 October.
2112191282000924837.line: Xi's speech marking 90 years since the Red Army's Long March, framed as a lesson for today.
2112191282000924837.says: PRC accounts relayed Xi Jinping's 22 October speech commemorating the 90th anniversary of the Red Army's Long March. The framing ties the Communist Party's history to present goals, quoting Xi's call for "new achievements on the new Long March" and his line that only by remembering history can China create a brighter future.

sample.text: President Xi Jinping called for new achievements on the new Long March as China commemorates the 90th anniversary of the victory of the Red Army's Long March on Thursday. "Only by remembering history can we create a brighter future," said Xi…

2112207369706835997.name: China–Africa summitry
2112207369706835997.desc: Xi Jinping's four principles on African 'hotspot issues', his four-point proposal on mining cooperation, and readouts of his talks with the leaders of Botswana and Togo.
2112207369706835997.line: Xi's mid-October meetings with African leaders, pitched as China offering principles for Africa's problems.
2112207369706835997.says: Embassies in Africa amplified Xi Jinping's 13 October meetings with the leaders of Togo and Botswana. They highlighted Xi's "four principles" for outside involvement in African conflicts and a four-point proposal on China–Africa mining cooperation, presenting China as a constructive partner.

sample.text: President Xi Jinping put forward four principles for the constructive participation of relevant parties in addressing African hotspot issues.

2114203099862909073.name: Taiwan and the UN seat (25 Oct)
2114203099862909073.desc: Posts on 25 October marking 'Taiwan Retrocession Day' with a video titled 'The Way Home', and the 55th anniversary of UN General Assembly Resolution 2758.
2114203099862909073.line: 25 October anniversaries used to assert that Taiwan belongs to China and the PRC alone represents China at the UN.
2114203099862909073.says: On 25 October PRC accounts marked two anniversaries together: Taiwan's 1945 handover from Japanese rule, which they call "Taiwan's Restoration", and UN Resolution 2758 of 1971, which seated the PRC at the UN. The framing claims both events settle Taiwan's status as part of China, and praises China's 55 years at the UN.

sample.text: This 25 October marks 55 years since the restoration of China's lawful seat at the United Nations. Over these 55 years, China has upheld the central role of the United Nations and has worked tirelessly for a fairer and more…
